neighbours.label: a rank label from a fixed ordered set: playing-card ranks (Ace, J, K) and Greek-letter star designations (Alpha Orionis, Beta Pictoris)
fire: In this solitaire you build each pile down from King to Ace.
The slot's low symbols are 10, J, Q, K and A in bright colors.
The brightest star in Lyra is Vega, also called Alpha Lyrae.
Astronomers found a planet around the young star Beta Pictoris.
He drew a Queen and then another Ace from the deck.
The second brightest star in the constellation is Beta Centauri.
Aces are high, so an Ace beats a King in this game.
Look east to find Gamma Cassiopeiae in the W shape.
quiet: In this solitaire you build each pile by matching colors.
The slot's low symbols are fruits and bells in bright colors.
The brightest star in Lyra is Vega, a blue-white giant.
Astronomers found a planet around a young star in Pictor.
He shuffled the deck and dealt two cards to each player.
The second brightest star in the constellation is very hot.
Cards are dealt face down, so nobody sees them in this game.
Look east to find the W shape of Cassiopeia tonight.

notes: Card: 'from Ace to King', 'A, K, Q, J', '(Alpha Orionis)', 'gamma', 'Beta Pictoris'. The - pole is the suits/elements side (spades, hearts, Earth sign, fire). Very sparse.
